Lewis Base-Switched [3 + 3] and [4 + 2] Annulation Reactions of
δ‑Acetoxy Allenoates with Cyclic N‑Sulfonyl Imines: Divergent
Synthesis of Functionalized α‑Pyridyl Acetates and Teraryl Sca ﬀolds
Sanjeeva K. Arupula, Asif Ali Qureshi, and K. C. Kumara Swamy *
Cite This: J. Org. Chem. 2020, 85, 4130 −4144 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: Under metal-free conditions, δ-acetoxy allenoates
react with cyclic N-sulfonyl imines (sulfamidate imines/sulfonyl
imines) to a ﬀord functionalized 2-pyridinyl acetates ( α-pyridyl
acetates) or teraryl motifs by a simple Lewis base switch. Thus,
while DBU/Na
2CO3 combination-directed [3 + 3] annulation
involves sulfonyl elimination via O −So rC −S bond cleavage,
aﬀording 2-pyridinyl acetates, Ph 3P-catalyzed [4 + 2] annulation
leads to functionalized teraryls via Mannich coupling and C −N
bond cleavage with retention or cleavage of the sulfamoyloxy group
depending on the reaction conditions.
■ INTRODUCTION
Allenes have been well recognized as key building blocks in
organic synthesis. 1 During the past decade, the Lewis base-
catalyzed annulation of allenoates has emerged as one of the
most powerful tools for the synthesis of structurally divergent
carbo- and heterocyclic motifs.
2 Subsequent to the early
example of phosphine-catalyzed (3 + 2) annulation of
butadienoate with electron-de ﬁcient ole ﬁns reported by
Zhang and Lu,
3 research on the Lewis base-catalyzed
annulations of a variety of allenoates have been extensively
studied. For example, phosphine-catalyzed [3 + 2],
4 [4 + 1], 5
[4 + 2], 6 and [4 + 4] 7 cycloaddition reactions were developed
as eﬀective approaches for the construction of a wide variety of
carbo/heterocyclic rings and medicinally signi ﬁcant natural
compounds.8 In addition to phosphines, tertiary amines have
also been extensively investigated as nucleophilic catalysts to
facilitate numerous annulation reactions of allenoates. For
instance, [4 + 2], [3 + 3], and other annulations of allenoates
have been reported for the as sembly of heterocycles.
9
Moreover, β′/δ-acetoxy allenoates have also been identi ﬁed
as e ﬀective annulation partners under Lewis base catalysis by
Tong as well as others (cf. Scheme 1).10 An important point to
be noted in these organocatalytic reactions is the di ﬀerence
between phosphines and amines as organocatalysts leading to
distinctly di ﬀerent products in several cases. 11
The α-pyridyl acetates as well as teraryl sca ﬀolds with
hydroxyl/sulfonamide functionality have been found in a
variety of natural and pharmaceutical compounds.
12 These
scaﬀolds are also explored as versatile intermediates to
construct complex molecules. 13 A literature survey reveals
that a fair amount of research is focused on α-pyridyl acetates
(cf. Scheme 2 a)14 and teraryls. 15 However, these strategies
have several drawbacks such as the requirement of expensive
transition metal catalysts, high temperature, unstable reagents,
and strong bases. Hence, a less expensive metal-free approach
for the synthesis of such structural motifs is in urgent demand.
Despite the substantial progress made on acetoxy allenoates,
there is no report of annulation reaction between δ-acetoxy
allenoates and bi-nucleophilic cyclic N-sulfonyl imines.
16 A
combination of acetoxy allenoates and cyclic N-sulfonyl imines
may lead to 2-pyridinyl acetates and unsymmetrical o-teraryls

with a hydroxyl, sulfonamide, or sulfamoyloxy unit, which are
otherwise di ﬃcult to obtain by reported procedures. A recent
elegant report from Tong ’s group disclosed the synthesis of
multisubstituted biaryl motifs from δ-acetoxy allenoates that
requires a tosyloxy group at the second position of β-keto ester
and use of Ph 3P( Scheme 2b).17 In this context, our interest in
allene chemistry 1f,18 motivated us to explore these substrates
for new Lewis base-switched annulations. It may be noted that
sulfamidate imines/sulfonyl imines can act as nucleophiles
(active methylene group) as well as electrophiles (imine
moiety). Our work reported herein embodies divergent
annulations of δ-acetoxy allenoates with cyclic N-sulfonyl
imines (sulfamidate imines/sulfonyl imines) under metal-free
conditions and involves a simple Lewis base switch to a ﬀord
(i) a new class of α-pyridyl acetates (2-pyridinyl acetates) by
[3 + 3] annulation via SO
2 elimination and (ii) functionalized
o-teraryls by [4 + 2]-benzannulation through C −N bond
cleavage ( Scheme 2 c). While the reaction with sulfamidate
imines involves O −S bond cleavage, the one with sulfonyl
imines entails C −S bond cleavage.
■ RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
Initially, 4-methyl cyclic sulfamidate imine 1a and δ-acetoxy
allenoate 2a were chosen as model substrates. As depicted in
Table 1 , we tested the reaction of 1a (1.0 equiv) with 2a (1.2
equiv) by using DABCO (0.20 equiv) in toluene at rt (25 °C).
However, only a trace amount of desired α-pyridyl acetate 3aa
was observed (entry 1). The yield could be enhanced to 31%
by using 50 mol % DABCO (entry 2). Addition of Na
2CO3
(1.0 equiv) improved the yield of 3aa to 43% (entry 3); further
increase to 56% was achieved by performing the reaction at 50
°C (entry 4). Use of 1.5 or 2.0 equiv Na
2CO3 augmented the
yield to 62% (entries 5 and 6). Among the bases (DBU, Et 3N,
DIPEA, and DMAP) checked, DBU turned out to be the best
(entry 7, also see Table S1). The additives K
2CO3 and t-BuOK
in place of Na 2CO3 produced 3aa in slightly lower yield
(entries 8 and 9). Among the screened solvents (cf. Table S1),
toluene was the best, a ﬀording the desired product 3aa in 79%
yield (entry 7). There was no quanti ﬁable di ﬀerence in the
isolated yields with increased time (entry 10). Interestingly,
use of PPh
3 (TPP) in place of DBU provided the entirely
diﬀerent product 4aa (53%; entry 11). To increase the yield of
the latter product 4aa, we performed the reaction between 1a
and 2a at di ﬀerent temperatures. Surprisingly, the S −O bond-

cleaved product 5aa was obtained in 73% yield at 80 °C (entry
12); by the exclusion of Na 2CO3, the yield of this product
could be enhanced further (entry 13). Pleasingly, at rt, we
obtained sulfomoyloxy carboxylate 4aa exclusively, with an
isolated yield of 73% (entry 14); increasing the reaction time
was not required here also (entry 15). In the absence of TPP
and Na
2CO3, we did not observe any reaction even after 24 h.
Coming to the substrate scope, as depicted in Table 2 , δ-
acetoxy allenoates possessing di ﬀerent functionalities (OMe,
Cl, and NO 2) on the phenyl ring furnished the 2-pyridinyl
acetates in good to high yields ( 3aa−3ad). Heterocyclic
allenoates 2e and 2f also readily underwent [3 + 3] annulation
with 1a to a ﬀord the desired pyridyl acetates 3ae and 3af in
good yield (67 −69%). The allenoate 2b with the electron-
donating group (4-OMe) on the phenyl ring delivered the
pyridine cores in slightly higher yield than the allenoate 2d
containing an electron-withdrawing group (NO
2). Delightedly,
this protocol was e ﬃcient in the reaction of a nucleophilic
partner containing electron-poor ( −Br; 1c) as well as electron-
rich (Me; 1b) functionalities with the δ-acetoxy allenoates 2a−
2d,a ﬀording the corresponding α-pyridyl acetates ( 3ba−3bd
and 3ca−3cc)i n6 7 −83% yield. In the case of precursor 1d,
we had to use 1 mole equiv of DBU to get the best yield of
3da−3dc (72−7 6 % ) .I ti sr e m a r k a b l et h a tt h ec y c l i c
sulfamidate imine 1e with a naphthyl group also enabled us
to obtain the corresponding acetate 3ea in 69% yield under our
protocol.
To conﬁrm the feasibility of the present [3 + 3] and [4 + 2]
annulations, scale-up experiments were carried out between 1a
(1.0 mmol) and 2b (1.2 mmol) under the optimized
conditions ( Scheme 3 ). The reactions worked well, and we
isolated the corresponding products with good yields.
As mentioned above, the [4 + 2] annulation product,
terphenyl sulfomoyloxy carboxylate 4aa, was obtained in good
yield by performing the reaction of 1a with 2a at rt in the
presence of Ph
3P (cf. Table 1 , entry 14). By employing the
same conditions and using cyclic sulfamidate imines ( 1b−1c),
we could obtain sulfomoyloxy carboxylates 4ba and 4ca in
decent yields ( Table 3). Satisfyingly, the heterocyclic allenoate
2f also a ﬀorded the annulated product 4af in good yield
(65%).
The phenolic terphenyl 5aa must have formed by the
elimination of −SO2(NH2) moiety from 4aa. This could be
proven readily by heating compound 4aa in toluene that
aﬀorded 5aa quantitatively by S −O bond cleavage. Since such
phenolic teraryls are useful sca ﬀolds in organic synthesis, 19 we
prepared the analogous of multisubstituted phenolic teraryls
5aa−5ad in one pot in 75 −85% yields. Precursors 1b and 1c
also provided the [4 + 2] annulation products 5ba−5bd and
5ca −5cd in good yields. Even the ethyl substituted
oxathiazine-2,2-dioxide 1d delivered the product 5da in 72%
yield. Heterocyclic allenoates 2e and 2f also participated
eﬃciently to a ﬀord the products 5ae and 5af. All these are
depicted in Table 3 .
In contrast to the sulfamidate imines 1a−1e that contain an
OSO
2 moiety, leading to products 3 with a phenolic −OH, the
sulfonyl imines 6a−6b have the sulfur directly bonded to the
arene. Hence, in reactions using 6a−6b, the SO 2 moiety has to
be eliminated to obtain products similar to 3. Our initial
attempt to treat 6a with 2a under the [3 + 3] annulation
protocol (cf. Table 1 , entry 7) only led to a trace amount
(<5%) of 7aa; at 100 °C, 25% yield was obtained. Finally, we
found that 1 mole equiv of DBU provided 7aa in 71% yield at
100 °C/12 h. As shown in Table 4 , 6a−6b showed good
reactivity with 2b−2c and produced 2-pyridinyl acetates 7ab−
7ac and 7ba−7bc in acceptable yields. Remarkably, the
heterocyclic acetoxy allenoates 2e−2f also participated
eﬃciently in this [3 + 3] annulation to produce 7ae−7af in
decent yields. In an e ﬀort to identify/isolate intermediates for
this [3 + 3] annulation, we performed the reaction between 6b
and 2b using 1.5 equiv of DBU at 60 °C. Pleasingly, after 12 h,
we isolated the fused dihydro-pyridine 8bb in 74% yield whose
structure was conﬁrmed by X-ray crystallography. This product
8bb could be converted to 2-pyridinyl acetate 7bb (1H NMR/
HRMS evidence) in toluene under basic conditions at 100 °C.

Based on this observation, we conclude that the 2-pyridinyl
acetates 7 are formed by the elimination of −SO2 group (C−S
bond cleavage) from the fused dihydro-pyridine motifs of type
8bb.
Inspired by the above success with cyclic sulfamidates in [4
+ 2] annulation, we tested this protocol with sulfonyl imines
6a−6b (Table 5 ). Pleasingly, terphenyls 9aa−9ad, 9af, and
9ba that retain the sulfonamide group are obtained in high to
excellent yields. Thus, in contrast to compounds of type 5, the
sulfonyl group is intact here since sulfur is directly attached to
the arene ring.
Based partly on the previous literature,
20 plausible pathways
for the above [3 + 3] and [4 + 2] annulations are shown in
Scheme 4. We could observe peaks assignable to intermediates
A1, A2/A3, B1, and B2 by checking crude reaction mixtures
using ESI-HRMS (see the Supporting Information ). Initially,
the δ-acetoxy allenoate 2a undergoes S
N2′ attack with Lewis
base (DBU 20d or TPP) to deliver the electrophilic
intermediate A1 or B1 by the elimination of acetate anion.
In the [3 + 3] annulation, A1 is likely to be less electrophilic
(at β-carbon), rendering Michael addition (route i) less
favorable than DBU elimination. Hence, the cationic
intermediate A1 undergoes a second S
N2′ attack (route ii)
rapidly with carbanion 1a′ generated by deprotonation of 1a to
aﬀord intermediate A2. Subsequently, ring closure of A2 via 6-
exo-dig cyclization leading to A3 followed by SO 2 elimination/
aromatization o ﬀers 2-pyridinyl acetate 3aa. The likely role of
Na2CO3 in this reaction is to scavenge the acetic acid formed
and to facilitate SO 2 elimination.21 In the [4 + 2] annulation,
the α-carbon in the intermediate B1 is more electrophilic. The
driving force for Michael addition is ylide formation with 1a′
to give B2 via route iii (more favorable than route iv). This is
followed by 1,2-proton shift to a ﬀord B3 that undergoes TPP
elimination, leading to the diene B4 via route v. Then, B4
undergoes intramolecular vinylogous Mannich coupling 22
followed by C −N bond cleavage/aromatization, a ﬀording
sulfamoyloxy-terphenyl-carboxylate 4aa. Finally, 4aa produces
5aa by the cleavage of O −S bond upon heating. Another
pathway, which involves more number of steps, is also possible
for the phosphine catalysis. Thus, ylide B2 may involve in
Mannich coupling via route vi to a ﬀord B3′ that undergoes

■ CONCLUSIONS
In this study, we have described new Lewis base-switched [3 +
3] and [4 + 2] annulation protocols involving cyclic N-sulfonyl
imines and δ-acetoxy allenoates generating functional pyridinyl
acetates and terphenyls, respectively, under metal-free
conditions. While in amine-mediated [3 + 3] annulation,
cyclic N-sulfonyl imines act as C/N donors and a ﬀord 2-
pyridyl acetates via double S
N2′−SN2′ attack followed by aza-
Michael addition and SO 2 elimination/aromatization, in TPP-
catalyzed [4 + 2] annulation, cyclic N-sulfonyl imines act as C/
C donors and deliver terphenyl sca ﬀolds via a S N2′ attack
followed by Michael addition, intramolecular direct vinylogous
Mannich coupling, and C −N bond cleavage/aromatization.
■ EXPERIMENTAL SECTION
General Methods. All the reactions were carried out either under
an inert atmosphere or air. All required chemicals were procured from
Aldrich or local manufacturers and used as such without further
puriﬁcation, unless noted. Melting points have been recorded on an
MR-visual melting range apparatus and are uncorrected. The 1H and
13C NMR spectra were recorded using 5 mm tubes on a 400 and 500
MHz NMR spectrometer [ ﬁeld strengths: 400/100 or 500/125 MHz,
respectively] in CDCl 3 solution (unless speci ﬁed otherwise) with
shifts referenced to TMS ( 1H, 13C = 0). Data for 1H and 13C NMR
are reported as a chemical shift ( δ, ppm). All J values are in Hz. The
infrared spectra were recorded using the attenuated total re ﬂection
technique on a Fourier-transform infrared spectrophotometer. The
mass spectra were recorded using HRMS (ESI-TOF analyzer)
equipment. Crystallographic data were collected on a X-ray
diﬀractometer system using Mo-K α radiation ( λ = 0.71073 Å)
radiation. Structures were solved and re ﬁned using standard methods.
Thin-layer chromatography (TLC) was performed on silica/alumina
plates, and components were visualized under iodine/UV light at 254
nm. Column chromatography was performed on silica gel (100 −200
mesh); for the column elution process, hexane-EtOAc mixture was
used as the eluent, unless otherwise stated.

(ii) General Procedure for the Synthesis of Compounds
3aa−3ea. A Schlenk tube was charged with cyclic sulfamidate imine
1 (0.20 mmol), δ-acetoxy allenoate 2 (0.24 mmol), Na 2CO3 (0.30
mmol), and 1.5 mL of toluene. Subsequently, DBU (0.10 mmol) in
0.5 mL of toluene was added, the mixture was stirred at 50 °C (oil
bath) for the stipulated time, and the reaction progress was monitored
using TLC. After completion of the reaction, the mixture was
quenched by adding water (10 mL). The aqueous layer was extracted
with ethyl acetate (3 × 5 mL). Then the combined organic layer was
washed with brine, dried over anhydrous Na
2SO4, and concentrated
under reduced pressure. The crude product was then puri ﬁed by silica
gel column chromatography using ethyl acetate/hexane (10:90) as the
eluent.
Ethyl 2-(6-(2-Hydroxyphenyl)-4 -phenylpyridin-2-yl)acetate

Lewis Base-Switched [3 + 3] and [4 + 2] Annulation Reactions of
δ‑Acetoxy Allenoates with Cyclic N‑Sulfonyl Imines: Divergent
Synthesis of Functionalized α‑Pyridyl Acetates and Teraryl Sca ﬀolds
Sanjeeva K. Arupula, Asif Ali Qureshi, and K. C. Kumara Swamy *
Cite This: J. Org. Chem. 2020, 85, 4130 −4144 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: Under metal-free conditions, δ-acetoxy allenoates
react with cyclic N-sulfonyl imines (sulfamidate imines/sulfonyl
imines) to a ﬀord functionalized 2-pyridinyl acetates ( α-pyridyl
acetates) or teraryl motifs by a simple Lewis base switch. Thus,
while DBU/Na
2CO3 combination-directed [3 + 3] annulation
involves sulfonyl elimination via O −So rC −S bond cleavage,
aﬀording 2-pyridinyl acetates, Ph 3P-catalyzed [4 + 2] annulation
leads to functionalized teraryls via Mannich coupling and C −N
bond cleavage with retention or cleavage of the sulfamoyloxy group
depending on the reaction conditions.
■ INTRODUCTION
Allenes have been well recognized as key building blocks in
organic synthesis. 1 During the past decade, the Lewis base-
catalyzed annulation of allenoates has emerged as one of the
most powerful tools for the synthesis of structurally divergent
carbo- and heterocyclic motifs.
2 Subsequent to the early
example of phosphine-catalyzed (3 + 2) annulation of
butadienoate with electron-de ﬁcient ole ﬁns reported by
Zhang and Lu,
3 research on the Lewis base-catalyzed
annulations of a variety of allenoates have been extensively
studied. For example, phosphine-catalyzed [3 + 2],
4 [4 + 1], 5
[4 + 2], 6 and [4 + 4] 7 cycloaddition reactions were developed
as eﬀective approaches for the construction of a wide variety of
carbo/heterocyclic rings and medicinally signi ﬁcant natural
compounds.8 In addition to phosphines, tertiary amines have
also been extensively investigated as nucleophilic catalysts to
facilitate numerous annulation reactions of allenoates. For
instance, [4 + 2], [3 + 3], and other annulations of allenoates
have been reported for the as sembly of heterocycles.
9
Moreover, β′/δ-acetoxy allenoates have also been identi ﬁed
as e ﬀective annulation partners under Lewis base catalysis by
Tong as well as others (cf. Scheme 1).10 An important point to
be noted in these organocatalytic reactions is the di ﬀerence
between phosphines and amines as organocatalysts leading to
distinctly di ﬀerent products in several cases. 11
The α-pyridyl acetates as well as teraryl sca ﬀolds with
hydroxyl/sulfonamide functionality have been found in a
variety of natural and pharmaceutical compounds.
12 These
scaﬀolds are also explored as versatile intermediates to
construct complex molecules. 13 A literature survey reveals
that a fair amount of research is focused on α-pyridyl acetates
(cf. Scheme 2 a)14 and teraryls. 15 However, these strategies
have several drawbacks such as the requirement of expensive
transition metal catalysts, high temperature, unstable reagents,
and strong bases. Hence, a less expensive metal-free approach
for the synthesis of such structural motifs is in urgent demand.
Despite the substantial progress made on acetoxy allenoates,
there is no report of annulation reaction between δ-acetoxy
allenoates and bi-nucleophilic cyclic N-sulfonyl imines.
16 A
combination of acetoxy allenoates and cyclic N-sulfonyl imines
may lead to 2-pyridinyl acetates and unsymmetrical o-teraryls

with a hydroxyl, sulfonamide, or sulfamoyloxy unit, which are
otherwise di ﬃcult to obtain by reported procedures. A recent
elegant report from Tong ’s group disclosed the synthesis of
multisubstituted biaryl motifs from δ-acetoxy allenoates that
requires a tosyloxy group at the second position of β-keto ester
and use of Ph 3P( Scheme 2b).17 In this context, our interest in
allene chemistry 1f,18 motivated us to explore these substrates
for new Lewis base-switched annulations. It may be noted that
sulfamidate imines/sulfonyl imines can act as nucleophiles
(active methylene group) as well as electrophiles (imine
moiety). Our work reported herein embodies divergent
annulations of δ-acetoxy allenoates with cyclic N-sulfonyl
imines (sulfamidate imines/sulfonyl imines) under metal-free
conditions and involves a simple Lewis base switch to a ﬀord
(i) a new class of α-pyridyl acetates (2-pyridinyl acetates) by
[3 + 3] annulation via SO
2 elimination and (ii) functionalized
o-teraryls by [4 + 2]-benzannulation through C −N bond
cleavage ( Scheme 2 c). While the reaction with sulfamidate
imines involves O −S bond cleavage, the one with sulfonyl
imines entails C −S bond cleavage.
■ RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
Initially, 4-methyl cyclic sulfamidate imine 1a and δ-acetoxy
allenoate 2a were chosen as model substrates. As depicted in
Table 1 , we tested the reaction of 1a (1.0 equiv) with 2a (1.2
equiv) by using DABCO (0.20 equiv) in toluene at rt (25 °C).
However, only a trace amount of desired α-pyridyl acetate 3aa
was observed (entry 1). The yield could be enhanced to 31%
by using 50 mol % DABCO (entry 2). Addition of Na
2CO3
(1.0 equiv) improved the yield of 3aa to 43% (entry 3); further
increase to 56% was achieved by performing the reaction at 50
°C (entry 4). Use of 1.5 or 2.0 equiv Na
2CO3 augmented the
yield to 62% (entries 5 and 6). Among the bases (DBU, Et 3N,
DIPEA, and DMAP) checked, DBU turned out to be the best
(entry 7, also see Table S1). The additives K
2CO3 and t-BuOK
in place of Na 2CO3 produced 3aa in slightly lower yield
(entries 8 and 9). Among the screened solvents (cf. Table S1),
toluene was the best, a ﬀording the desired product 3aa in 79%
yield (entry 7). There was no quanti ﬁable di ﬀerence in the
isolated yields with increased time (entry 10). Interestingly,
use of PPh
3 (TPP) in place of DBU provided the entirely
diﬀerent product 4aa (53%; entry 11). To increase the yield of
the latter product 4aa, we performed the reaction between 1a
and 2a at di ﬀerent temperatures. Surprisingly, the S −O bond-

could be enhanced further (entry 13). Pleasingly, at rt, we
obtained sulfomoyloxy carboxylate 4aa exclusively, with an

was not required here also (entry 15). In the absence of TPP
and Na

Coming to the substrate scope, as depicted in Table 2 , δ-
acetoxy allenoates possessing di ﬀerent functionalities (OMe,
Cl, and NO 2) on the phenyl ring furnished the 2-pyridinyl
acetates in good to high yields ( 3aa−3ad). Heterocyclic
allenoates 2e and 2f also readily underwent [3 + 3] annulation
with 1a to a ﬀord the desired pyridyl acetates 3ae and 3af in
good yield (67 −69%). The allenoate 2b with the electron-
donating group (4-OMe) on the phenyl ring delivered the
pyridine cores in slightly higher yield than the allenoate 2d
containing an electron-withdrawing group (NO
2). Delightedly,
this protocol was e ﬃcient in the reaction of a nucleophilic
partner containing electron-poor ( −Br; 1c) as well as electron-
rich (Me; 1b) functionalities with the δ-acetoxy allenoates 2a−
2d,a ﬀording the corresponding α-pyridyl acetates ( 3ba−3bd
and 3ca−3cc)i n6 7 −83% yield. In the case of precursor 1d,
we had to use 1 mole equiv of DBU to get the best yield of
3da−3dc (72−7 6 % ) .I ti sr e m a r k a b l et h a tt h ec y c l i c
sulfamidate imine 1e with a naphthyl group also enabled us
to obtain the corresponding acetate 3ea in 69% yield under our
protocol.
To conﬁrm the feasibility of the present [3 + 3] and [4 + 2]
annulations, scale-up experiments were carried out between 1a
(1.0 mmol) and 2b (1.2 mmol) under the optimized
conditions ( Scheme 3 ). The reactions worked well, and we
isolated the corresponding products with good yields.
As mentioned above, the [4 + 2] annulation product,
terphenyl sulfomoyloxy carboxylate 4aa, was obtained in good
yield by performing the reaction of 1a with 2a at rt in the
presence of Ph
3P (cf. Table 1 , entry 14). By employing the
same conditions and using cyclic sulfamidate imines ( 1b−1c),
we could obtain sulfomoyloxy carboxylates 4ba and 4ca in
decent yields ( Table 3). Satisfyingly, the heterocyclic allenoate
2f also a ﬀorded the annulated product 4af in good yield
(65%).
The phenolic terphenyl 5aa must have formed by the
elimination of −SO2(NH2) moiety from 4aa. This could be
proven readily by heating compound 4aa in toluene that
aﬀorded 5aa quantitatively by S −O bond cleavage. Since such
phenolic teraryls are useful sca ﬀolds in organic synthesis, 19 we
prepared the analogous of multisubstituted phenolic teraryls
5aa−5ad in one pot in 75 −85% yields. Precursors 1b and 1c
also provided the [4 + 2] annulation products 5ba−5bd and
5ca −5cd in good yields. Even the ethyl substituted
oxathiazine-2,2-dioxide 1d delivered the product 5da in 72%
yield. Heterocyclic allenoates 2e and 2f also participated
eﬃciently to a ﬀord the products 5ae and 5af. All these are
depicted in Table 3 .
In contrast to the sulfamidate imines 1a−1e that contain an
OSO
2 moiety, leading to products 3 with a phenolic −OH, the
sulfonyl imines 6a−6b have the sulfur directly bonded to the
arene. Hence, in reactions using 6a−6b, the SO 2 moiety has to
be eliminated to obtain products similar to 3. Our initial
attempt to treat 6a with 2a under the [3 + 3] annulation
protocol (cf. Table 1 , entry 7) only led to a trace amount
(<5%) of 7aa; at 100 °C, 25% yield was obtained. Finally, we
found that 1 mole equiv of DBU provided 7aa in 71% yield at
100 °C/12 h. As shown in Table 4 , 6a−6b showed good
reactivity with 2b−2c and produced 2-pyridinyl acetates 7ab−
7ac and 7ba−7bc in acceptable yields. Remarkably, the
heterocyclic acetoxy allenoates 2e−2f also participated
eﬃciently in this [3 + 3] annulation to produce 7ae−7af in
decent yields. In an e ﬀort to identify/isolate intermediates for
this [3 + 3] annulation, we performed the reaction between 6b
and 2b using 1.5 equiv of DBU at 60 °C. Pleasingly, after 12 h,
we isolated the fused dihydro-pyridine 8bb in 74% yield whose
structure was conﬁrmed by X-ray crystallography. This product
8bb could be converted to 2-pyridinyl acetate 7bb (1H NMR/
HRMS evidence) in toluene under basic conditions at 100 °C.

8bb.
Inspired by the above success with cyclic sulfamidates in [4
+ 2] annulation, we tested this protocol with sulfonyl imines
6a−6b (Table 5 ). Pleasingly, terphenyls 9aa−9ad, 9af, and
9ba that retain the sulfonamide group are obtained in high to
excellent yields. Thus, in contrast to compounds of type 5, the
sulfonyl group is intact here since sulfur is directly attached to
the arene ring.
Based partly on the previous literature,
20 plausible pathways
for the above [3 + 3] and [4 + 2] annulations are shown in
Scheme 4. We could observe peaks assignable to intermediates
A1, A2/A3, B1, and B2 by checking crude reaction mixtures
using ESI-HRMS (see the Supporting Information ). Initially,
the δ-acetoxy allenoate 2a undergoes S
N2′ attack with Lewis
base (DBU 20d or TPP) to deliver the electrophilic
intermediate A1 or B1 by the elimination of acetate anion.
In the [3 + 3] annulation, A1 is likely to be less electrophilic
(at β-carbon), rendering Michael addition (route i) less
favorable than DBU elimination. Hence, the cationic
intermediate A1 undergoes a second S
N2′ attack (route ii)
rapidly with carbanion 1a′ generated by deprotonation of 1a to
aﬀord intermediate A2. Subsequently, ring closure of A2 via 6-
exo-dig cyclization leading to A3 followed by SO 2 elimination/
aromatization o ﬀers 2-pyridinyl acetate 3aa. The likely role of
Na2CO3 in this reaction is to scavenge the acetic acid formed
and to facilitate SO 2 elimination.21 In the [4 + 2] annulation,
the α-carbon in the intermediate B1 is more electrophilic. The
driving force for Michael addition is ylide formation with 1a′
to give B2 via route iii (more favorable than route iv). This is
followed by 1,2-proton shift to a ﬀord B3 that undergoes TPP
elimination, leading to the diene B4 via route v. Then, B4

5aa by the cleavage of O −S bond upon heating. Another
pathway, which involves more number of steps, is also possible
for the phosphine catalysis. Thus, ylide B2 may involve in

■ CONCLUSIONS
In this study, we have described new Lewis base-switched [3 +
3] and [4 + 2] annulation protocols involving cyclic N-sulfonyl
imines and δ-acetoxy allenoates generating functional pyridinyl
acetates and terphenyls, respectively, under metal-free
conditions. While in amine-mediated [3 + 3] annulation,
cyclic N-sulfonyl imines act as C/N donors and a ﬀord 2-
pyridyl acetates via double S
N2′−SN2′ attack followed by aza-
Michael addition and SO 2 elimination/aromatization, in TPP-
catalyzed [4 + 2] annulation, cyclic N-sulfonyl imines act as C/
C donors and deliver terphenyl sca ﬀolds via a S N2′ attack
followed by Michael addition, intramolecular direct vinylogous
Mannich coupling, and C −N bond cleavage/aromatization.
■ EXPERIMENTAL SECTION
General Methods. All the reactions were carried out either under
an inert atmosphere or air. All required chemicals were procured from
Aldrich or local manufacturers and used as such without further
puriﬁcation, unless noted. Melting points have been recorded on an
MR-visual melting range apparatus and are uncorrected. The 1H and
13C NMR spectra were recorded using 5 mm tubes on a 400 and 500
MHz NMR spectrometer [ ﬁeld strengths: 400/100 or 500/125 MHz,
respectively] in CDCl 3 solution (unless speci ﬁed otherwise) with
shifts referenced to TMS ( 1H, 13C = 0). Data for 1H and 13C NMR
are reported as a chemical shift ( δ, ppm). All J values are in Hz. The
infrared spectra were recorded using the attenuated total re ﬂection
technique on a Fourier-transform infrared spectrophotometer. The
mass spectra were recorded using HRMS (ESI-TOF analyzer)
equipment. Crystallographic data were collected on a X-ray
diﬀractometer system using Mo-K α radiation ( λ = 0.71073 Å)
radiation. Structures were solved and re ﬁned using standard methods.
Thin-layer chromatography (TLC) was performed on silica/alumina
plates, and components were visualized under iodine/UV light at 254
nm. Column chromatography was performed on silica gel (100 −200
mesh); for the column elution process, hexane-EtOAc mixture was
used as the eluent, unless otherwise stated.
